title: AI-Powered Monitoring & Analysis of Bitcoin Transaction Traffic
description:
• Background Bitcoin's pseudonymous, peer-to-peer design lets criminal actors move, layer, and cash out illicit funds - ransomware payments, darknet-market proceeds, extortion, and laundering - while evading traditional financial surveillance.
The objective of problem statement is to design and build a complete system (offline) that ingests bulk Bitcoin transaction/network metadata (in CSV/JSON/XML), correlates network-layer (IP/port/timing) observations with blockchain-layer (wallet/TXID/amount) data, and applies AI/ML to detect anomalies, cluster entities, and generate prioritized, explainable investigative leads.
• Description i.Challenge Objectives- • Ingest & parse a bulk metadata dataset (timestamp, src/dst IP & port, TXID, input/output wallet addresses, amounts, fee, script type).
• Build an entity/transaction graph linking IPs, wallets, and transactions.
• Implement AI/ML detection use case (see Section 4) with a working model - not just rules.
• Generate a ranked, explainable alert list (why a wallet/transaction was flagged, with a confidence score).
• Present findings via a simple dashboard or link-analysis visualization.
ii.Suggested AI/ML Focus Areas Attach Table Here of AI/ML Focus Areas iii.Dataset: Parameters & Synthetic Generation Participants will work with a synthetic dataset modelled on real Bitcoin P2P/transaction fields (no real seized or live-intercept data will be provided). Minimum fields: timestamp, src_ip, dst_ip, src_port, dst_port, txid, input_addresses[], output_addresses[], input_amounts[], output_amounts[], geo_country/asn (integrate open source downloadable Geo IP database).
• Expected Solution • Workable complete offline solution for linux platform.
• Working prototype (code repo) with ingestion, correlation, and AI/ML model.
• Short technical write-up: approach, model choice, and explain ability method.
• Dashboard/visualization showing flagged entities and evidence for each flag.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, blockchain applied to a transportation & logistics problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Transportation & Logistics. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on blockchain, model. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 19/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AI-Powered Monitoring & Analysis of Bitcoin Transaction Traffic

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that links network-level clues (IP addresses, timing) with blockchain transaction data to spot suspicious Bitcoin activity, cluster related wallets together, and generate a ranked, explainable list of investigative leads for analysts.
overview.why_it_matters: Bitcoin's pseudonymity lets criminals launder ransomware payments and darknet proceeds while evading traditional financial surveillance. Combining network and blockchain signals directly helps investigators cut through that.
pain_points: Bitcoin's pseudonymous design lets criminal actors move and launder funds while evading traditional surveillance.
Network-layer and blockchain-layer data aren't currently correlated in one investigative system.
Manual investigation of transaction graphs doesn't scale to real transaction volumes.
overview.background: Bitcoin's pseudonymity enables illicit fund movement, and correlating network-layer (IP/timing) with blockchain-layer (wallet/transaction) data could surface investigative leads that neither layer alone reveals.
overview.whats_being_asked: An offline system ingesting bulk Bitcoin transaction/network metadata, correlating network and blockchain layers, applying AI/ML to detect anomalies and cluster entities, and generating explainable, prioritized investigative leads with a dashboard.
expected_solution: Bulk metadata ingestion (timestamp, IP/port, TXID, wallet addresses, amounts).
Entity/transaction graph linking IPs, wallets, and transactions.
AI/ML-based anomaly detection and entity clustering (working model, not just rules).
Ranked, explainable alert list with confidence scores, plus dashboard visualization.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Very High. Correlating network-layer and blockchain-layer data for entity clustering and anomaly detection is genuine, active blockchain-forensics research territory.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires graph-based entity resolution, genuine ML-based anomaly detection (not just rule-based flagging, explicitly required), and explainability together, substantial technical depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine blockchain forensics and graph-ML expertise together, a narrow, technical field.

innovation.note: Network-to-blockchain correlation for entity clustering is genuine, sophisticated blockchain forensics territory.

invention.note: Graph-based entity resolution plus genuine ML anomaly detection (explicitly not just rules) is substantial technical depth.

technical_feasibility.note: Explicitly framed as offline with bulk metadata, achievable using constructed or public blockchain transaction data.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly supports real financial crime investigation capability.

architecture.note: Graph construction, ML detection, and explainable ranking together, real but well-understood integration.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with graph analytics and ML experience. The explicit requirement for a working ML model (not just rules) is a real bar worth taking seriously, don't submit a purely rule-based system relabeled as AI.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified technical requirements (entity graph, working ML model, explainable ranked output) give clear, concrete deliverables.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a purely rule-based flagging system without genuine ML modeling would fail the PS's explicit requirement for 'a working model - not just rules'.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Ensure your anomaly detection genuinely uses a trained ML model (e.g. graph neural network, clustering algorithm, or anomaly-detection model) rather than hardcoded threshold rules, this is explicitly required, not optional.

idea_0_4: Source or construct real/realistic Bitcoin transaction metadata (public blockchain data is accessible; network-layer correlation data needs construction).
Design your entity/transaction graph schema linking IPs, wallets, transactions.
Split: one person on graph construction, one on the ML anomaly-detection/clustering model.
prototype_4_22: Build your entity/transaction graph from ingested metadata.
Build your genuine ML-based anomaly detection or entity-clustering model.
Start explainability logic connecting model output to human-readable reasoning.
integration_22_30: Connect graph, ML detection, and explainability into one coherent pipeline.
Test with embedded suspicious patterns (structured layering, rapid wallet-hopping) to confirm detection works.
Build the ranked alert dashboard/link-analysis visualization.
polish_30_36: Polish the dashboard for genuine investigator usability.
Rehearse presenting a specific flagged case with full explainable reasoning.
Prepare to confirm your detection is genuinely ML-based, not rule-based, if asked directly.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show a specific flagged wallet/transaction with clear, explainable reasoning tracing back to your genuine ML model's output (not a hardcoded rule), that combination of real ML detection and honest explainability is exactly what the PS explicitly asks for.

strengths: Very well-specified requirements give clear, concrete deliverables.
weaknesses: Real network-to-blockchain correlation data needs careful, realistic construction.
Explicit 'working model, not rules' requirement raises the technical bar meaningfully.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: ML-weighted, given the explicit requirement for genuine model-based detection.
team_fit.approach: Prioritize building a genuine trained model early, don't default to rule-based flagging as a fallback that fails the stated requirement.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard graph construction and ML model scaffolding.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing genuinely meaningful anomaly-detection features for blockchain forensics (not generic anomaly detection), that requires real domain understanding of illicit transaction patterns.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A superficial rule-based system dressed up with AI terminology would fail the PS's explicit requirement and likely underperform a genuinely trained model on real detection tasks.

data_resource_availability.status: Public blockchain transaction data is accessible; realistic network-layer correlation data needs construction, clearly labeled as constructed.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Construct a synthetic dataset combining real public blockchain data with realistic simulated network-layer metadata.

judge_qna.question: Is your detection genuinely a trained ML model, or rule-based flagging?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Confirm directly that you built and trained a genuine model, describing the specific architecture and what it learned, this requirement was explicit in the problem statement.
judge_qna.follow_up: What features did your model find most predictive of suspicious activity?

judge_qna.question: How does your system correlate network-layer and blockchain-layer data specifically?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific correlation approach, timing alignment, IP-to-wallet linkage logic, and how that combined signal improves detection over either layer alone.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens when network-layer data is unavailable or unreliable for a given transaction?
